claims.text: The modified alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
SPS-processed equimolar WTaTiVZr has a multiphase microstructure consisting of a high-entropy BCC matrix and nanoscale secondary phases.
The secondary regions in WTaTiVZr are enriched in Ti or V/Zr.
The secondary-phase boundaries in WTaTiVZr are coherent or semi-coherent.
SPS-processed WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than SPS-processed pure tungsten under high-temperature service conditions.
SPS-processed WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than SPS-processed pure tungsten under high-temperature service conditions.
Secondary phases and their boundaries impede dislocation propagation.
Secondary-phase boundaries provide sites for heterogeneous dislocation nucleation.
Microstructural heterogeneities at the secondary phases locally activate additional slip systems.
The phase-boundary-mediated deformation produces more distributed and homogeneous plastic flow.
The secondary phases and their interfaces impede crack propagation.
The combination of dislocation nucleation and impeded dislocation motion delays strain localization and brittle failure.
Mixed-phase WTaTiVZr micropillars will display multi-stage yielding or a double-yield phenomenon.
WTaTiVZr will have a higher elevated-temperature strain to failure than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit more homogeneous dislocation activity than pure tungsten during elevated-temperature nanoindentation and micropillar compression.
WTaTiVZr is expected to show improved yield strength relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism remains valid while the SPS-induced multiphase microstructure is stable at high temperature.
Thermal coarsening or phase homogenization would diminish the plasticity and toughness advantages.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator describes the phase boundaries as coherent or semi-coherent, while the uncertainty field says the crystallographic nature of the secondary phases and boundaries is not fully characterized.
The conditions call for both tensile and compressive loading, but the specified intervention and falsification design include nanoindentation and micropillar compression only, with no tensile test.
